resources.string: Covers short-form feeds while leaving the rest of the app alone

BlockReels reads the on-screen layout of the apps you select in order to tell a short-form feed apart from the parts of the app you still want, such as messages and stories. Screen contents are never sent anywhere — the app has no internet permission.
Open a screen, then tap Dump
BlockReels cannot see which screen you are on until this is enabled.
If the toggle is greyed out, the install was classed as sideloaded. Open App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then try again. Installing with adb avoids this.
Adds a notification action that writes the current screen\'s layout to a file. Open Reels, dump, open Stories, dump, then diff the two — the ids in one and not the other are your detector.
Notifications are blocked, so the Dump button can\'t appear. Enable them in Settings → Apps → BlockReels → Notifications.
Turn on the accessibility service above — the Dump button is posted by it, so nothing appears until it\'s running.
Ready. Open the app you want to capture, swipe down from the top of the screen, and tap \"Dump screen\" on the BlockReels notification.
View ids unverified — capture the surfaces with dump mode and correct InstagramDetector before enabling.
If this stops rising, a detector has probably broken.
